compiled_state.title: [ticket-tracker-automation]: noisy auto-bug creation patterns produce tickets without actionable signal -> backlog cruft accumulates
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 944f622747fd60ff2883bd78cc0951530be664ed

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Automated bug creation should produce tickets that carry actionable signal — a specific defect to remediate, with reproduction steps and a clear remediation path. Auto-filed deferred review feedback should consolidate into actionable work items, not duplicate placeholders. plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md and plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/bug-report-template.md define this contract: every bug ticket has a non-empty Incident Overview and either actionable signal or explicit consolidation under the Consolidation Rule.

#### Actual Behavior

Two automated patterns are generating tickets that violate the signal/noise invariant. A 2026-05-24 local state audit of 556 open tickets during the Jira-sync re-brainstorm identified 84 such tickets (~15% of open local state). All 84 are being closed during the audit because they do not represent work.

**Pattern 1: Recurring tool-error telemetry bugs (4 tickets).** Auto-filed bug tickets whose title matches the regex `^Recurring tool error: <kind> \(<N> occurrences\)$`. They track runtime error frequencies — useful as metrics, not as work tickets. Each has empty description and no actionable defect. Examples:

- 2bdf-24d9-750c-4661: Recurring tool error: test_failure (514 occurrences)
- 3f69-64bf-aa0f-49ea: Recurring tool error: lint_failure (111 occurrences)
- 94e1-e071-df83-4b1f: Recurring tool error: edit_string_not_found (145 occurrences)
- f221-438c-d7e4-4725: Recurring tool error: read_file_does_not (135 occurrences)

**Pattern 2: PR-comment-deferred placeholder tasks (80 tickets).** /dso:respond-to-pr-comments creates one task per deferred review comment with title `[PR #<N>] Deferred review comment: <agreement>` and identical body. The audit found 80 of these from a single PR (#42), all titled `[PR #42] Deferred review comment: Agreed, we should track this separately.` — identical content, no individuating information, no link to the underlying comment's substance. Examples:

- 0de4-c367-1b86-435a
- 0ff8-8ff4-308d-40f1
- 1849-1a3b-9268-475c
- 3df6-... (and 77 more, all identical title and body)

The "Agreed, we should track this separately" pattern strips signal — the deferred comment's actual content is lost in the agreement boilerplate; only the meta-agreement remains as 80 duplicate tickets pointing back at "PR #42" with zero individuating information.

Combined effect: 84 noise tickets out of 556 open (~15%); 84 of 472 native-local outbound-sync candidates (~18%) would have propagated to Jira during the new reconciler's first pass if not caught. The audit eliminates them; the upstream patterns will re-introduce them on the next PR-comment-defer or tool-error cluster.

### 3. Action History

- 2026-05-24: /dso:brainstorm session for Jira-sync remediation re-brainstorm
- Spike (live derivable diff against DIG) produced 472 outbound creates — investigated as too high
- Local state audit categorized cruft: 4 telemetry bugs + 80 PR-comment-deferred placeholders
- Both categories auto-closed under user authorization

### 5. Skills and Workflows

Two upstream sources to remediate:

(a) The runtime tool-error tracker that auto-files "Recurring tool error" bugs. Recommended remediation: convert to metrics emission (log line, /dso:debug-everything aggregation, dashboard tile) instead of ticket creation. If ticket creation is retained, threshold-gate at a much higher count (e.g., >1000 occurrences per error class) and consolidate per-kind into a single rolling ticket.

(b) /dso:respond-to-pr-comments deferred-comment handling. Recommended remediation: preserve the original comment content verbatim in the ticket body instead of dropping it for an agreement boilerplate; consolidate multiple deferrals from a single PR into ONE tracking ticket with per-comment bullets (apply the existing Consolidation Rule from create-bug SKILL.md §"Consolidation Rule"); never create more than one deferral ticket per (PR, comment-class) tuple.

### 6. Logs

Audit output sample (Cat B head):
```
=== Cat B samples (top 5 of 80) ===
  0319-1871-9152-4a9f: PR comment deferred: Agreed, we should track this separately.
  0de4-c367-1b86-435a: [PR #42] Deferred review comment: Agreed, we should track this separately.
  0ff8-8ff4-308d-40f1: [PR #42] Deferred review comment: Agreed, we should track this separately.
  1303-1360-96e8-467a: PR comment deferred: Agreed, we should track this separately.
  1849-1a3b-9268-475c: [PR #42] Deferred review comment: Agreed, we should track this separately.
```

comments.body: Classification: compound bug — 2 independent sub-issues detected: (1) error-sweep.sh auto-creates bug tickets with low threshold (50 occurrences), generating noise tickets; (2) respond-to-pr-comments defer handler creates duplicate tickets when defers are processed concurrently (race condition in consolidation logic). Both are behavioral + llm-behavioral (Pattern 2 involves skill guidance gap). Score: Pattern 1 = behavioral (threshold/script), Pattern 2 = llm-behavioral (SKILL.md + script). Routing to cluster investigation mode with known root causes from audit.
comments.author: Test

comments.body:
Investigation complete. Root causes identified:

Pattern 1 (Recurring tool error tickets): error-sweep.sh THRESHOLD=50 was too low, creating noise tickets for common operational errors. Fixed by raising to THRESHOLD=500. This prevents tickets for error categories with <500 occurrences.

Pattern 2 (Duplicate defer tickets from respond-to-pr-comments): The defer handler _handle_defer() consolidates multiple defers from the same PR into one ticket via a tag lookup (pr-<N>-deferred). This consolidation fails when Step 4 calls are parallelized — all 80 calls see no existing ticket before any of them creates one. Fixed by adding explicit sequential processing requirement in SKILL.md Step 4.

Fix applied:
- plugins/dso/scripts/end-session/error-sweep.sh: THRESHOLD 50 → 500
- plugins/dso/skills/respond-to-pr-comments/SKILL.md: Added CRITICAL sequential processing note in Step 4
- tests updated to reflect new threshold
